chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Being courteous to people is a third of the intellect.

key_terms.العقل: The intellect, reason, practical wisdom — in Shia tradition, a faculty encompassing moral and social discernment, not merely cognitive ability
key_terms.مجاملة: Cordiality, courteous treatment, friendly conduct — the gracious and respectful manner of dealing with others

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about kindness to people and its relation to intellect?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that treating people with kindness and cordiality constitutes one-third of a person's intellect. This profound maxim frames social grace not as a superficial courtesy but as a fundamental component of rational, virtuous conduct. In the classical Islamic understanding, 'aql (intellect) encompasses practical wisdom, moral discernment, and the capacity to act rightly in society — and the Imam places human-to-human cordiality as integral to that capacity.
